pr_title: Refactor OS exit code to be `EXIT_SUCCESS` by default
pr_body:
We've had a number of issues and PRs in the past few years following #38929, which aimed at solving #30207. The issue was that Godot defaulted to a success exit code, so if any error condition that cause interruption of the process failed to set the error code properly, it would go unnoticed in systems that rely on error codes (like CI to mark the job as failed).

This caused a number of situations where Godot would wrongly report a failure code on exit, even though it's not failing. This was most prominent with the Linux headless build used on CI, leading to issue #62898 which was fixed by #67421. And a number of other PRs to fix special cases for command line options which were still wrongly treated as success or failure (e.g. `--help` and `--version` have been special cased).

But now Godot can run headless on any platform, so since the fix in #67421 was Linux specific, it doesn't work when doing e.g. command line import and exports on Windows or macOS. PRs #81518 and #83479 aim to work this around but they're again only workarounds, and we've been piling workarounds long enough already.

Time to go back to the drawing board and fix our exit code propagation.

So after discussing with @mihe and @reduz I drafted this to see how to clean things up, go back to `EXIT_SUCCESS` as the default exit code, and see how to ensure that all early exits/aborts will properly go through a pass that sets `EXIT_FAILURE` or another non-zero error code.

We still need to dig through all the reported issues and PRs, closed and open, and make sure that this doesn't regress in any situation. There's some good discussion in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81518#discussion_r1320836149 which should be continued here. We need to make test cases so we can have confidence about this approach.

To be clear, this may well turn out to be a wrong approach too, as @touilleMan flagged in #81518. We'll have to see if we can solve the other types of problems this approach would raise in a better way, or stick to defaulting to `EXIT_FAILURE` but make it more robust.

Some details about the `main.cpp` changes:

- `Main::setup` early exits (failure or `--help`/`--version`) now
  consistently return `EXIT_FAILURE` or `EXIT_SUCCESS` on all platforms,
  instead of 255 on some and a Godot Error code on others.
- `Main::start` now returns the exit code, simplifying the handling of early
  failures.
- `Main::iteration` needs to explicit set the exit code in OS if it errors
  out.
- Web and iOS now properly return `OS::get_exit_code()` instead of 0.
---

- Supersedes #81518.
- Supersedes #83479 (and doesn't seem to introduce the bug @Calinou outlined in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/83479#pullrequestreview-1740045770).
- Should fix #83449, but needs testing.
- Fixes #88055.
- Reverts #67421.
- Doesn't seem to reintroduce #30207.
  * I tested scenarios where no main scene is defined, or the main scene points to a missing file.
  * I'm not sure how to reproduce the actual problem from the OP in #30207. It seemed to be a bug in export templates in 3.1 days, trying the same project on 3.5 or 4.3 doesn't terminate the Godot process, so there's no reason for the exit code to be non-zero.
  * Help welcome to identify other test cases for this.
- Doesn't reintroduce #62898 on Linux.
  * Worth testing on Windows and macOS too, help welcome there as I mostly use Linux.
- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7557 (doesn't solve it).
- There might be more issues/PRs to consider while checking if this PR is a good approach. Please help me by linking them :)

CC @touilleMan @mihe @reduz @dalexeev @InfinitiesLoop @dreed-sd @ePirat
pr_comments:
> Doesn't seem to reintroduce [When the game crashes it still exits with code 0 #30207](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/30207) (needs more testing, I only tested the scenario where no main scene is defined, or it's pointing at a missing file).

I haven't tried this with an exported build, like the repro in that issue mentions, but when running a similar scene with just the editor binary (using the console wrapper on Windows) I do seem to end up with an `EXIT_SUCCESS` despite the script parse error.

Here's the MRP I'm using for that: [ScriptErrorExitCode.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14515191/ScriptErrorExitCode.zip)

Script parsing errors are special-cased though, by the looks of it, so maybe it just is what it is and it actually shouldn't trigger an `EXIT_FAILURE`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b94c80e9aff2a4f363ae6d8e2bbe837aa5876bc/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L2828-L2831

A crude solution to that could otherwise be to just stick a `OS::get_singleton()->set_exit_code(EXIT_FAILURE)` inside of [`_err_print_error`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b94c80e9aff2a4f363ae6d8e2bbe837aa5876bc/core/error/error_macros.cpp#L84-L102) if there isn't already a failure exit code set, and maybe skip it if it's a warning perhaps. It might be somewhat aggressive to treat every single error as a failure of the entire process, but I suppose an error is an error, and signaling that one has happened using the exit code doesn't seem all that unreasonable.

You would with that of course be able to overwrite the exit code with `SceneTree.quit` at some later point, which may or may not be desirable.

TL;DR: No change of behavior from this PR on that test case or #30207.

> I haven't tried this with an exported build, like the repro in that issue mentions, but when running a similar scene with just the editor binary (using the console wrapper on Windows) I do seem to end up with an `EXIT_SUCCESS` despite the script parse error.
> 
> Here's the MRP I'm using for that: [ScriptErrorExitCode.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14515191/ScriptErrorExitCode.zip)

The behavior in my PR seems to be the same as in `master` / 4.3-dev4. The script error doesn't cause the termination of the process, the scene still loads and runs gracefully. So it's expected to me that the exit code is `EXIT_SUCCESS`.

The issue reported by the OP in #30207 was specific to exported projects. When running with an editor binary, the scene doesn't fail to load, so Godot doesn't exit, and thus the exit code when closing Godot manually is 0. In the exported project, the scene completely fails to load and Godot stops. That's when the exit code should be a failure.

Here's how the MRP from #30207 behaves with a Linux debug export from 3.1.1:
```
$ ./Crashing.x86_64 
OpenGL ES 3.0 Renderer: AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi, gfx1103_r1, LLVM 17.0.6, DRM 3.57, 6.7.7-200.fc39.x86_64)
SCRIPT ERROR: GDScript::load_byte_code: Parse Error: Expected end of statement after expression.
   At: res://Node.gdc:10.
ERROR: load_byte_code: Method/Function Failed, returning: ERR_PARSE_ERROR
   At: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:785.
ERROR: load: Condition ' err != OK ' is true. returned: RES()
   At: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2168.
ERROR: _load: Failed loading resource: res://Node.gdc
   At: core/io/resource_loader.cpp:285.
ERROR: poll: res://Node.tscn:3 - Parse Error: [ext_resource] referenced nonexistent resource at: res://Node.gd
   At: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:440.
ERROR: load: Condition ' err != OK ' is true. returned: RES()
   At: core/io/resource_loader.cpp:208.
ERROR: _load: Failed loading resource: res://Node.tscn
   At: core/io/resource_loader.cpp:285.
ERROR: start: Failed loading scene: res://Node.tscn
   At: main/main.cpp:1739.
WARNING: cleanup: ObjectDB Instances still exist!
   At: core/object.cpp:2095.
ERROR: clear: Resources Still in use at Exit!
   At: core/resource.cpp:425.
$ echo $?
0
```

Here's how it behaves with a Linux debug export from 4.3-dev4. Unlike 3.1.1, it doesn't terminate the process, and the scene plays gracefully, just without its script. So I have to close the window manually, and the error code is 0, as I would expect. So it's a different scenario to the one in 3.1.1.
```
$ ./Crashing.x86_64 
Godot Engine v4.3.dev4.official.df78c0636 - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.3.267 - Forward+ - Using Device #1: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT (RADV NAVI33)

SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Expected end of statement after expression, found "Identifier" instead.
          at: GDScript::reload (res://Node.gdc:9)
ERROR: Failed to load script "res://Node.gdc" with error "Parse error".
   at: load (modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2824)
$ echo $?
0
```

> A crude solution to that could otherwise be to just stick a `OS::get_singleton()->set_exit_code(EXIT_FAILURE)` inside of [`_err_print_error`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b94c80e9aff2a4f363ae6d8e2bbe837aa5876bc/core/error/error_macros.cpp#L84-L102) if there isn't already a failure exit code set, and maybe skip it if it's a warning perhaps. It might be somewhat aggressive to treat every single error as a failure of the entire process, but I suppose an error is an error, and signaling that one has happened using the exit code doesn't seem all that unreasonable.

In my experience, non-zero exit codes only happen when an error is unrecoverable and causes the program to terminate. It's not a sign that _some_ errors happened at some point during execution. So I don't think this should be changed, at least not by default. This could be considered as an option for folks who really want their project never to raise an error (like `-Werror` for C++ compilers), but that's not what was asked for in #30207 or subsequent issues IMO. So this is proposals territory.

What we need to find is situations where are error causes the Godot process to terminate. It can be outright crashes (segfault/abort), or maybe other kind of script conditions that would cause a termination - but it might well be that since 3.1.1, we ironed things out so that script errors never cause a program termination.
Does this PR affect the ability to resolve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83042?

Did some more testing (and fixed a bug while at it #89234), I think it's already relatively solid, so taking out of draft.
Still needs more extensive testing and review before merging of course.

issue_context.title: Exit code 1 after importing in headless mode with --quit
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.1.1.stable.official [bd6af8e0e]

### System information

macOS 13.0.1 - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Apple M1 Max - Apple M1 Max (10 Threads)

### Issue description

When running godot in headless mode to import a project for the first time (no .godot folder yet), it seems to succeed in that there are no errors, but the exit code is 1. This causes CI actions (e.g. a github action) to assume the step failed, preventing us from being able to produce exports as part of CI. For example, when using this github action, it will fail since it can't get passed the import step: https://github.com/marketplace/actions/godot-export

```
dreed ~/git/GodotTest
$ rm -rf .godot/

dreed ~/git/GodotTest
$ g project.godot --headless -e --quit
Godot Engine v4.1.1.stable.official.bd6af8e0e - https://godotengine.org

WARNING: Custom cursor shape not supported by this display server.
     at: cursor_set_custom_image (servers/display_server.cpp:480)
WARNING: Blend file import is enabled in the project settings, but no Blender path is configured in the editor settings. Blend files will not be imported.
     at: _editor_init (modules/gltf/register_types.cpp:73)

dreed ~/git/GodotTest
$ echo $?
1
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new blank project on MacOS with Godot 4.1.x
2. Close the Godot editor
3. Delete the .godot folder
4. Run godot in headless mode with -e --quit: `godot project.godot --headless -e --quit`
5. Echo the exit code with `echo $?`
6. --> Exit code is 1 even though there were no apparent errors

I tried this with --verbose as well and there's a lot more info provided, but still nothing that looks like an error or even a warning. 

### Minimal reproduction project

[GodotTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/12920043/GodotTest.zip)
comments:
- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83042.

This doesn't occur on my end with 4.2.dev 42425baa5 (Linux) when using `--quit` on the project manager or editor on a project, regardless of whether it already has a `.godot/` folder or not.

Commands I've tried:

```bash
godot --quit
godot --quit /tmp/4/project.godot --editor  # `--editor/-e` is implied when specifying a path to `project.godot`.
godot --quit /tmp/4/project.godot
godot --quit --path /tmp/4/ --editor
godot --headless --quit
godot --headless --quit /tmp/4/project.godot --editor  # `--editor/-e` is implied when specifying a path to `project.godot`.
godot --headless --quit /tmp/4/project.godot
godot --headless --quit --path /tmp/4/ --editor
```

To check for the origin of the exit code, I recommend searching for instances of `set_exit_code(`, `quit(` and `_exit_editor(` in the codebase.
I believe the platform matters. It maybe specific to MacOS Godot. CI that needs to sign exports with xcode need to be on a Mac (if I am not mistaken), so not easy to work around.

I added logging to `OS::set_exit_code` and `SceneTree::exit`, nothing ever calls it on this code path. So I believe it is using exit code 1 simply because it's the default value and nothing ever sets it: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fd33c7b32f54e9ac3d346be718618575338cd7ef/core/os/os.h#L59

~I don't know the code well enough to know where/what should be setting `EXIT_SUCCESS`, unless someone has an idea I'd be happy to submit a PR~

Edit: It would seem it simply needs to be set explicitly prior to setting exit = true in main. All other code paths set the exit code explicitly, only this one didn't. I have submitted a PR

review_comments: CC @adamscott @Faless - I changed this for consistency with other platforms, but I don't know if this can have unwanted implications.
